## Profile

Quantitative health researcher with backgrounds in clinical psychology, epidemiology, and medical statistics. My research interests include psychiatric and perinatal epidemiology, child and adolescent health, longitudinal research, and health inequalities.

## Education

- **M.Sc. Epidemiology**, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz, 2025–present
- **M.Sc. Clinical Psychology and Psychotherapy**, University of Göttingen, completed 2025
- **B.Sc. Psychology**, University of Göttingen, completed 2022

## Selected research experience

- **ManyBabies Consortium** — Infant habituation, neonatal imitation, screen time, and multi-analyst research
- **Global Mental Health Project** — Coordination of the German research team within an international collaboration spanning more than 80 countries
- **Boston Children’s Hospital / Harvard Medical School** — Longitudinal research on mania symptoms in the Adolescent Brain Cognitive Development Study
- **Cambridge Policy Research Group** — Cross-national research on online choice architecture across more than 25 countries
- **Toronto Metropolitan University** — Mitacs Globalink research internship in the Addictions and Mental Health Laboratory


## Quantitative methods

- Data preparation and reproducible analysis in R
- Regression and mixed-effects models
- Longitudinal analysis
- Latent class and growth mixture modelling
- Causal inference
- Machine learning and prediction
- Multi-analyst and collaborative research

## Selected publication

## Looking ahead

My long-term goal is to conduct a PhD in psychiatric or perinatal epidemiology using large-scale cohort or register data. I am always interested in meeting researchers working in these areas and contributing to collaborative projects.
